# Gradient Discontinuity: Logbook

Split from `boundary-characterization/` (gradient angle change and gradient-cell alignment analysis).

## Motivation

Measures how the sys gradient direction changes at combinatorial boundaries. Two analyses: (1) gradient angle change at the first boundary crossing, and (2) correlation between gradient boundary distance and cell width from per-facet profiling.

## Status

**Complete (2026-03-27).** 873 gradient rows, 2 figures. Data generated by `boundary-characterization/run.rs`.

## How to run

Data is generated by the boundary-characterization binary:
```bash
cd crates/ && cargo run -p exp-combinatorial-cells --release --bin cell-boundary-characterization
```

Then run the analysis:
```bash
cd crates/exp-combinatorial-cells/gradient-discontinuity/
uv run analyze.py
```

## Results (from combinatorial-anatomy, 2026-03-27)

### Gradient angle change at boundaries

| Metric | Median | Max |
|--------|--------|-----|
| Gradient angle change | 0.002 deg | 70.2 deg |

(gradient JSONL, all 873 rows, boundary_gradient_angle.png)

Most boundaries cause negligible gradient change. Large angle changes (up to 70 deg) occur at orbit-switching boundaries (3% of crossings).

### Gradient-cell alignment

Correlation between gradient boundary distance and narrowest per-facet cell width: r = 0.518 (gradient_cell_alignment.png). The gradient doesn't target narrow cell directions.

## Related experiments

- **boundary-characterization** -- generates the data files this experiment analyzes
- **cell-widths** -- per-facet cell width data used for gradient-cell alignment analysis
